title: Dante Vale
summary: Dante Vale, as the top operative of the Huntik Foundation, is an expert treasure hunter, sleuth, and martial artist. Originally acting as a hired detective, he took to leading the team of Lok Lambert, Sophie Casterwill, Zhalia Moon, and later Den Fears on a mission to track down the missing Foundation operative and father of Lok, Eathon Lambert, and to retrieve the Legendary Titans. He has developed a close bond with his Titans, particularly his trusted Caliban and Solwing.

sections.heading: History
sections.text:
]]
When he was young, Dante Vale met Metz, who recognized Dante's potential to be a Seeker. Through Metz' tutelage, Dante learned about magic and Titans. Dante's first Amulet to bond to, that of Solwing, was found all by himself while spending time in Turkey. [Ladies' Choice] Dante was also given a Caliban Amulet by Metz, though Dante took over a year to be able to invoke and master the Meso-Titan due to Caliban's immense power. Initially, Dante was only able to keep Caliban summoned for about a minute, though Dante increased this time through training. [Huntik.com] His friendship with Metz also found Dante working alongside Eathon Lambert and Simon Judeau. [Huntik.com/Profiles] As a teenager, he trained intensively under Metz' friend Master Storm in China alongside Lin Storm, with whom he formed a close friendship. [Lok's Leadership]

Some years later, Dante found another Caliban Amulet in South America, during one of his most dangerous missions for the Huntik Foundation. [Caliban Amulet (GP Card)] Dante kept this a secret, with everyone believing he possessed simply the one Caliban, who had become his most distinctive Titan. [The Mission] 

Dante later gained an Ignatius Amulet while on an expedition to a volcano in Chile. As Ignatius Amulets were common in this country, both Dante and another Seeker acquired one during this expedition. Another Meso-Titan, Dante was able to control much faster after learning how to control Caliban, though Ignatius' flares occasionally would set something, such as buildings, on fire. Three water Titans were once needed to put Ignatius out. [Huntik.com]

In his youth, Dante also crossed paths with Montehue, a student of the history of war and fellow treasure hunter, with the pair instantly forming a competitive but nonetheless friendly rivalry. Whilst racing up a mountain, Dante secretly slipped a Tolivane Amulet into Montehue's pocket as a way of keeping things fair. After saving Montehue from falling to his death, Dante left a lasting impression on him, and introducing him to the world of Seekers. The pair's competitive friendship spanned many years, with the pair eventually becoming close friends through working together to use Mjolnir to defeat Ymir in the Temple of Thor and, later, fighting side by side against the Professor in King Solomon's mines. [Two Powers Become One] [To Be Together]

Dante was manipulated by the Professor into giving him the Rings of Behemoth and Tao so that he could perform a ritual to summon Lord Casterwill's Titan of Immortality, Overlos which would end the Curse of the Legendary Titans, saving Metz's life. Dante also gave him back his Caliban Amulet, which the Professor had originally used to save Metz' life at the Temple of Tecobai. Dante saw it as a way of repaying old debts, truly believing that Simon could save Metz one last time. However, it turned out to be a trick, as the Professor had much more evil intentions with the three Legendary Titans. This broke Dante mentally, and caused him to go into a state of shock and grief. [S1E25] Lok therefore had to lead the mission to stop the Professor's plan. Dante eventually managed to recover from his stupour and save Zhalia from two Undergolem Titans. He tried to put right his mistake by helping Lok to stop the Professor and battle the three Legendary Titans. He summoned Archwarder, disrupting the Professor's control over Overlos, allowing Lok to use Dendras and command Overlos to banish himself and the other three Legendary Titans to the Spirit World. [S1E26]

 of Caliban]]
During a mission to rescue Clements from the Ring of Arc, Dante entered a dreamworld, created by Arc, the Legendary Titan of Fate. Here, Dante had a vision of his own death with Zhalia and his friends crying at his grave. Despite being visibly haunted by this, as to not worry anybody, he kept it to himself and told no one. [The Legendary Titan of Fate][Lok's Leadership][The Guardian of Yonaguni]

Dante was left saddened when Zhalia chose to leave the Huntik team, adamant she plays to her strengths and infiltrate the Blood Spiral to fight them from the inside. [Zhalia's Mission] Using Zhalia's Logosbook, the pair communicated with one another. [Sophie on Trial]

In the Vault of Hernán Cortés, Dante managed to beat Wilder in recovering the Ring of the Legendary Titan of Dimensions, Umbra, the Shadow Jaguar. [The Power of Umbra]

Deeply shaken by the vision of his future and with the threat of the Blood Spiral looming, Dante returned to train under Master Storm in China. After learning the Copykind spell, he used Umbra to join his team in the Castle of Vlad Dracul. Using Copykind to mimic Ignatius' flames, he caused the Heart of Vlad Dracul to overload and injure Tantras. [Lok's Leadership]

During the final battle at the Spiral Mark, Dante was able to defeat Rassimov one on one while helping Lok and Sophie destroy Legion. However, the Betrayer revealed that he had faked the last prophecies of Nostradamus, and in attempting to destroy the Mark, the team had activated it and sent the Red Comet hurtling towards Earth. Realizing the time had come to fulfill his destiny that Arc had revealed, Dante died sacrificing himself to prevent the Red Comet from hitting the Earth. [The Spiral Mark]

Attempting to destroy his enemies' will to fight, the Betrayer revealed Dante's death to the Huntik Foundation and the Casterwill family, devastating Zhalia Moon, Metz, and Montehue. However, Lok, enraged at the Spirals' mocking of Dante's sacrifice, made a motivating speech, inspiring the Foundation to finish what Dante started, knowing he would have believed they could win the war without him. [Lok and the Betrayer]

During the Betrayer's ritual, Dante's ashes were teleported back to Earth by Umbra. By using the Copykind spell on Phoenix, the Legendary Titan of the Rebirth, just prior to his death, Dante was able to rise back to life from his ashes. Dante soon attempted to prevent the Betrayer from invoking the Nullifiers, battling him; however, his Hyperstrides couldn't keep up with the Betrayer's ability to fly, and he was knocked down and almost made immobile by the Betrayer's Shadowlock spell. Lok and Sophie, though, were quick to find a prophecy in Nostradamus' real writings, telling Dante to hold the Betrayer, which he did so with Stoneglove paired with Doublespell, allowing Lok to throw the Willblade at the Betrayer, revealing this weakness -- the Spiral mark on his back, thus enabling the team to finally stop the Betrayer. After the defeat of the Betrayer, Dante Vale became a member of the Huntik Foundation Council, leaving leadership of his old team to Lok Lambert. [Dante's Return]

sections.heading: Personality
sections.wikitext:
[[File:S1E42 Dante reflection.png|thumb|170px]]
A natural leader, Dante not only takes control of the situation, but also knows how to be a present mentor to his team. Through his years of experience and natural intelligence, he is an excellent tactician, often keeping several steps ahead of his opponents in [[the Organization]]. Enjoying the battle, he has an overall confident and sassy attitude when it comes to his combat skills, and often makes wisecracks while fighting. He manages to remain calm under stress and to adapt when unexpected events make his original plans not pan out. Fiercely loyal to his team, he will do anything in his power to protect his friends, such as trying to find a cure for Metz' curse. {{source|Absent Heroes}} As a result, he often sees the good in others before he sees the bad, such as being quick to forgive Zhalia for her betrayal of the team. This goodness, however, can also be his downfall, and even led to his falling for [[Simon Judeau|the Professor's]] deception and losing the [[Legendary Titans]].

As a leader and mentor for Sophie and Lok, he teaches them how to be Seekers. At first, he seemed to be a pro who doesn't do anything without getting a right payment, but it turned out that Dante is a friendly, helpful man who easily puts his whole heart in discovering secrets that interest him. He got involved in search for Eathon Lambert just because it was his job, but his feelings changed due to the growing bond with his young students. He developed a crush on Zhalia Moon and, despite her betrayal of the team, is willing to risk his life to protect her or to bring her back to the right side. Though he knows she will handle every job she is asked to do, he also gets worried every time she is in danger. They make a good team on the missions, fitting each other's style of fighting and perceiving what the other one is going to do.

sections.heading: Zhalia Moon
sections.text:
Dante initially knew of Zhalia as a fellow Foundation Seeker, and had a lot of respect for her skills, asking her to help the Huntik team in Prague after their first meeting. [S1E03] While other members of his team, particularly Sophie Casterwill, took a distrust to her, Dante saw her as reliable and trustworthy, letting her prove herself to the team by rescuing Peter in Rouen. [S1E04] Dante assured Zhalia that he trusted her after asking her to deliver DeFoe's Amulets which meant a great deal to her as nobody had ever told her that. [S1E10] Over time, the pair began to develop feelings for one another [S1E17], and despite Zhalia's betrayal of his team to Klaus, Dante understood her reasons and forgave her. [S1E17] After the explosion at her apartment, the pair almost kissed but were interrupted by Lok Lambert. [The Unseen Guide] They grew deeply protective of one another [S1E23] [S2E27] and Zhalia later admitted that Dante meant more to her than anything else in the world. [S1E25] 

When Zhalia chose to leave the team to infiltrate the Blood Spiral, Dante was deeply saddened but understood why she had to go. [S2E35] They stayed in touch by writing in a pair of Logosbook journals [S2E36] from which even Tantras could tell Zhalia cared for him a great deal. [S2E39] When Zhalia discovered Dante had sacrificed himself to stop the Red Comet, she was devastated. [S2E51] However, Dante wrote her a final message revealing his ultimate secret plan, and Zhalia was overjoyed when he rose from the ashes. [S2E52]

sections.heading: Grier
sections.wikitext:
[[File:S1E12 Grier Dante explosion.jpg|190px|thumb|Dante and Grier face off]]
Dante had an intense rivalry with [[Grier]], as both were powerful and charismatic Seekers harboring strong values. The more the two fought, the more they recognized that the other was fighting for the good of mankind, though both had very different ideas of this good. Extremely well-matched in physical combat, their conflicts were often resolved between their two gargantuan [[Titans]]: Dante's [[Metagolem]] and Grier's signature Titan, the bear-brawler, [[Breaker]], with this fighting rivalry reaching its peak when the two men battled it out on [[Sutos Island]]. Grier himself stated that he had waited his whole life to fight an opponent like Dante {{Source|Like Father, Unlike Son}} and Lok described their relationship to [[Den Fears]] as having been that of archenemies. {{source|An Ally from the Organization}}

sections.heading: Lok Lambert and Sophie Casterwill
sections.wikitext:
While initially Dante only accepted [[Sophie Casterwill|Sophie]] and [[Lok Lambert|Lok]]'s offer to help the latter find [[Eathon Lambert|his father]] as a paid job, he quickly bonded with them and was willing to take a [[Raypulse]] spell for [[Sophie Casterwill|Sophie]] the same day he took took the job. {{Source|The Casterwill Client}} Dante went as far as to reverse the roles and briefly return to his work as a private investigator to afford a trip relating to the search for [[Eathon Lambert]] and the [[Amulet of Will]] when Sophie's bank accounts were wiped. {{Source|All Work and No Pay}} Much like [[Metz]] was a mentor to Dante, he also taught Sophie and Lok many aspects of the [[Seekers|Seeker]] life; this is more noteworthy with Lok, who after charged with leading a mission complemented Dante's leadership. {{Source|Lok's Leadership}}
''Sophie, take care of Lok. Make sures he grows up just like his father.''
- Dante to Sophie before seemingly sacrificing himself to destroy the [[Red Comet]]

sections.heading: Abilities
sections.text:
have perfect telepathic communication]]
Dante is both a leader and tactician for his team, employing his intellect, experience, and knowledge of history to push his team forward. Having trained in both martial arts and the abilities of a Seeker, his combat style combines the two into a formidable force with either enhancing the other. Depending on the situation, he can use spells to augment his agility, enhance his martial arts, attack at a range, or provide shielding. All of this is combined with his impressive stamina and endurance, being able to withstand two days of non-stop walking without any food, water or sleep before finally passing out and still being able to invoke Titans and use spells shortly after. However, Dante was shown to be completely exhausted when he invoked Caliban, Metagolem and Behemoth within a short span of time. [S1E21] 

Over the years, Dante has amassed a vast and varied collection of Titans through his many adventures. He stores most of his Amulets in concealed safes and drawers inside his home. [The Casterwill Client] [S1E07] Although he relies primarily on a core group of Titans, he chooses to bring other Titans from his collection when specific missions call for different abilities. [S1E07] [S1E23] He has a close bond with several of his Titans due to the time spent training together, most notably his signature Titan, Caliban to whom he is now Powerbonded. [S2E35]

sections.heading: Trivia
sections.wikitext:
* Dante is 28 years old, according to ''[[Huntik Magazine]]'' [[Grand Dragon Leviathan (Comic)|Issue 9]] ''Seeker Community'' section, and the Huntik Sticker Album released by [[Panini]]. 
* In the first series' trailer, Dante and Zhalia's hair colors were switched, with Dante having blue hair instead.
* The show's artistic director, [[Simone Borselli]], revealed in an interview with ''Vanity Fair'' that Dante's appearance was modeled on that of the movie actor [[:wikipedia:Johnny Depp|Johnny Depp]].
* The name Dante is of Italian origin and means "steadfast." His last name may be derived from the word valley, the Latin word for "farewell," or the Portuguese phrase ''vale tudo'' which refers to full-contact and unarmed combat.
* Some of Dante's Titans share a Shakespearean theme, such as Caliban, Ariel and Oberon.
* In the episode [[Crawling the Catacombs]] we can see Dante opening a lock without a key in less than 25 seconds, which, to do it you need to have a lot of skill.
* Several of his Titans' names may be inspired by William Shakespeare's dramas, including [[Caliban]], [[Elf King Oberon]], and [[Ariel]].
* Show creator [[Iginio Straffi]] stated that if he had to be one of the show's characters, he would chose to be Dante. {{Extsource|1=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AjYWmvnOqQo&list=PL6NZlSvyFyQU-o6alH6pXfEqPNXEBFSQo|2=YouTube}}

[S1E17] After the explosion at her apartment, the pair almost kissed but were interrupted by Lok Lambert. [The Unseen Guide] They grew deeply protective of one another [S1E23] [S2E27] and Zhalia later admitted that Dante meant more to her than anything else in the world. [S1E25] 

When Zhalia chose to leave the team to infiltrate the Blood Spiral, Dante was deeply saddened but understood why she had to go. [S2E35] They stayed in touch by writing in a pair of Logosbook journals [S2E36] from which even Tantras could tell Zhalia cared for him a great deal. [S2E39] When Zhalia discovered Dante had sacrificed himself to stop the Red Comet, she was devastated. [S2E51] However, Dante wrote her a final message revealing his ultimate secret plan, and Zhalia was overjoyed when he rose from the ashes. [S2E52]

===Grier===

Dante had an intense rivalry with Grier, as both were powerful and charismatic Seekers harboring strong values. The more the two fought, the more they recognized that the other was fighting for the good of mankind, though both had very different ideas of this good. Extremely well-matched in physical combat, their conflicts were often resolved between their two gargantuan Titans: Dante's Metagolem and Grier's signature Titan, the bear-brawler, Breaker, with this fighting rivalry reaching its peak when the two men battled it out on Sutos Island. Grier himself stated that he had waited his whole life to fight an opponent like Dante [Like Father, Unlike Son] and Lok described their relationship to Den Fears as having been that of archenemies. [An Ally from the Organization]

=== Lok Lambert and Sophie Casterwill ===
While initially Dante only accepted Sophie and Lok's offer to help the latter find his father as a paid job, he quickly bonded with them and was willing to take a Raypulse spell for Sophie the same day he took took the job. [The Casterwill Client] Dante went as far as to reverse the roles and briefly return to his work as a private investigator to afford a trip relating to the search for Eathon Lambert and the Amulet of Will when Sophie's bank accounts were wiped. [All Work and No Pay] Much like Metz was a mentor to Dante, he also taught Sophie and Lok many aspects of the Seeker life; this is more noteworthy with Lok, who after charged with leading a mission complemented Dante's leadership. [Lok's Leadership]Sophie, take care of Lok. Make sures he grows up just like his father. 
 - Dante to Sophie before seemingly sacrificing himself to destroy the Red Comet

== Abilities ==
 have perfect telepathic communication]]
Dante is both a leader and tactician for his team, employing his intellect, experience, and knowledge of history to push his team forward. Having trained in both martial arts and the abilities of a Seeker, his combat style combines the two into a formidable force with either enhancing the other. Depending on the situation, he can use spells to augment his agility, enhance his martial arts, attack at a range, or provide shielding. All of this is combined with his impressive stamina and endurance, being able to withstand two days of non-stop walking without any food, water or sleep before finally passing out and still being able to invoke Titans and use spells shortly after. However, Dante was shown to be completely exhausted when he invoked Caliban, Metagolem and Behemoth within a short span of time. [S1E21] 

Over the years, Dante has amassed a vast and varied collection of Titans through his many adventures. He stores most of his Amulets in concealed safes and drawers inside his home. [The Casterwill Client] [S1E07] Although he relies primarily on a core group of Titans, he chooses to bring other Titans from his collection when specific missions call for different abilities. [S1E07] [S1E23] He has a close bond with several of his Titans due to the time spent training together, most notably his signature Titan, Caliban to whom he is now Powerbonded. [S2E35]

==Trivia==
* Dante is 28 years old, according to Huntik Magazine Issue 9 Seeker Community section, and the Huntik Sticker Album released by Panini. 
* In the first series' trailer, Dante and Zhalia's hair colors were switched, with Dante having blue hair instead.
* The show's artistic director, Simone Borselli, revealed in an interview with Vanity Fair that Dante's appearance was modeled on that of the movie actor Johnny Depp.
* The name Dante is of Italian origin and means "steadfast." His last name may be derived from the word valley, the Latin word for "farewell," or the Portuguese phrase vale tudo which refers to full-contact and unarmed combat.
* Some of Dante's Titans share a Shakespearean theme, such as Caliban, Ariel and Oberon.
* In the episode Crawling the Catacombs we can see Dante opening a lock without a key in less than 25 seconds, which, to do it you need to have a lot of skill.
* Several of his Titans' names may be inspired by William Shakespeare's dramas, including Caliban, Elf King Oberon, and Ariel.
* Show creator Iginio Straffi stated that if he had to be one of the show's characters, he would chose to be Dante.
